newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia amends intellectual property laws.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia amends intellectual property laws.

text.p: Indonesia's parliament has passed amendments to laws covering intellectual property rights, the official Antara news agency reported on Saturday.
Antara said the House of Representatives (DPR) on Friday passed amendments to a 1987 law on intellectual property rights, a 1989 law on patents, and a 1992 law on use of brand names.
Justice Minister Utojo Usman was quoted as saying the amendments would lead to stronger protection of intellectual property rights.

"The laws will protect intellectual property rights and increase innovation in technology, science and arts, and increase trade and investment in Indonesia," Usman was quoted by the Jakarta Post as telling parliament on Friday.
The Jakarta Post said the amendments were passed to make the three laws more consistent with the Agreement on Trade Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights, which Indonesia ratified in 1994.
The Jakarta Post said the copyright law was amended to clarify rules on assigning copyrights to inventions while the revised trademark law provides for tighter government protection of trademarks.
The amended patents law allows for the import of copies of a patented product if the original has never been produced in Indonesia, the newspaper said.
